rationale: `src/authoring/mod.rs#struct[PendingAssessment]` is a data holder for a judged assessment that is staged but not yet written. Its fields are the `subject` (which decides the evidence path), the evidence `record`, the `outcome` and the `usage` log. It is not a test, so `{test}` does not apply. It also isn't a root of the implementation of `requirements.authoring.persistence`. The code that does the persisting is already marked `{impl}` for that requirement: `impl[PendingAssessment]` and its `fn[persisted]`, plus `AuthoringSubject::evidence_path`, `record`, `configured_assessment`, and `stage_record` and `persist_record` in `batch.rs`. The struct is reached through those marked items, so it needs no `{impl}`. It does depend on what the requirement specifies. The requirement calls for writing the subject text, the determination and rationale, and the recorded inputs to the subject's evidence file, and for all three outcomes to be written as completed assessments. A change to the requirement could change what the struct has to carry. A `{cite}` is therefore the right role. The item has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement, so the citation is not redundant.

text: After one valid judgment, the harness MUST write the subject text, submitted
determination and rationale, and recorded inputs using the existing evidence
By default, it MUST write the subject's evidence file. With `--stdout`, it MUST
emit a single evidence JSON object followed by a newline to stdout and MUST NOT
create or change evidence files or directories. All three outcomes MUST be
